summary: Democrats are projected to control both chambers of Congress in January. After the defeats, Republican National Committee deputy KC Crosbie challenged party chair Joe Gruters and called for a review of what went wrong. Gruters defended his spending to committee members, and President Donald Trump backed him. The committee’s January vote will test whether Trump can keep his choice in charge of national party fundraising and campaign operations. In Congress, Democratic investigators face White House and Justice Department pressure as they prepare to lead committees. Axios reported that U.S. attorney Aaron Reitz asked Senator Elizabeth Warren to preserve records concerning her inquiries. The House vote to send Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee remains the latest verified step in that case. Pakistan says it is awaiting a U.S. reply to Iran’s proposals. Commerce released rules for licensing some remote uses of advanced U.S. chips. Alaska’s final results, recent immigration and tariff court orders, and the result of Venezuela’s latest talks remain open.
scope: Focused November 13–16 intake on congressional control, Republican leadership and 2028 positioning, congressional oversight, Iran diplomacy and advanced chip rules, with scheduled-outcome checks for all ten tracked issues. The latest immigration and tariff court orders, Cook’s hearing, Venezuela’s closing talks and actual Russia–Ukraine prisoner transfers remain unverified.
